producer_report.summary: Added a capability preflight, `crates/athena-core/src/preflight.rs`, as the mechanism for OLY-B-RUN-01. When a job is dispatched, the programs its checks run are looked up on Athena's own PATH through an injectable `ToolProbe`; the probe runs nothing. Each program is recorded as a line in the job record's `note`, in the prediction commit before any agent runs. A missing bare-name program closes the job `failed` with an `environment: preflight blocked:` reason that names the program, the checks that need it and a workaround plan. That is done by `stop_preflight` in run/pin.rs, called from `Athena::dispatch`. The stop leaves an earlier job's kept work alone. `Athena::retry` now retries the job that a preflight-stopped job had retried, so the retry chain stays true. Path programs and tools that only a relative PATH entry could supply are recorded as not probed and never block. docs/spec.toml gained the mechanism, owner and a measure ending `status: not shown` that names the test. CHANGELOG.md gained one line. 16 new tests all pass, each filtered by `capability_preflight`. Stubbing `preflight()`, dropping `resume: None`, or dropping `retry_target` each makes the matching test fail.

criteria_check.evidence: The preflight blocks only when SystemProbe returns Missing for a bare-name check program: path programs, relative-PATH tools and an unset PATH are `not probed` and never block (tests capability_preflight_lists_path_programs_as_not_probed, capability_preflight_relative_path_is_not_judged_missing). git and gh are not needs (capability_preflight_git_alone_and_gh_are_not_needs). No reading rule is touched, so no accepted reading is refused: the 0% figure is an estimate by reading, limited to this repository, whose checks all run `cargo`. Elsewhere an uninstalled check tool now stops the job instead of landing with a recorded pre-existing failure; that is intended and stated in the spec mechanism and CHANGELOG. The athena-cli lifecycle test baseline_failure_does_not_stop_the_job (path program) still passes.

open_issues: Departures from the accepted reading, as the plan decided: the probe looks the name up on PATH (runs nothing) instead of running `<tool> --version`; git is not probed on its own, because Athena runs it before the job record exists; the new dispatch and retry tests live in run/tests.rs and the retry link fix is in reading.rs, neither of which is on the deliverable list.
The per-program record is only in job.json `note`; no `athena status` line prints it (out of scope), so the measure ends `status: not shown`.

A preflight stop is an OtherEnvironment stop, so a drain does not end its run on it; while a bare-name check tool is missing, a drain keeps retrying items that need it. Making it end the drain like LowDisk is a follow-up outside these files.
The 0% newly refused estimate is by reading and holds only for this repository (all configured checks run `cargo`).
The last whole-workspace `cargo test --locked` was run in pieces, not as one command; the only failure (testkit scan) was fixed and that test reran green.
mistakes: My first mutation revert left two statements joined on one line, so cargo fmt --check failed until I ran cargo fmt. Fixed.
preflight.rs first used set_permissions in a test, which the testkit scan rejects. Replaced with athena_testkit::write_executable.
The first version of the blocked-job test pinned the reader count to 1; it is 2 because the reader runs again inside go. Removed that assertion.
learnings: athena-testkit has a scan (no_in_process_exec_writes) that rejects set_permissions or from_mode in test code anywhere in the workspace, untracked files included; use athena_testkit::write_executable.
A finished job's `prediction_commit` is the reading commit, not the dispatch commit; the dispatch commit is the outcome's `base_commit`, so tests read the dispatch-time job record from there.
The reader agent runs once more inside `go` after `ask`, so tests should not pin the reader count.
JobId has no `new`; tests build one with JobId::parse.
The full `cargo test --locked` takes longer than the 20-minute foreground limit (athena-core alone is about 7 minutes).
desires: A way to read the output of a background cargo run; policy blocks reads outside the working directory, so I reran in pieces.
A single quiet whole-workspace test command that finishes inside the foreground limit.
